Fleet V3 optional explicit account controls

This independently deliverable port extends the V3 native control/launcher. It
uses V3's serialized revision checks, immutable commits, compact receipts and
transactional SQLite tree store. It keeps the existing answer/resume attempt
record and conversation handling. No account service is loaded for an inherited
route. Existing Grok and default subscription routes require no setup here.

A lead may use fleet.control account-read to read retained route/default and
completion metadata. Explicit offset/limit pages include page.nextOffset;
expectedRevision detects intervening account control edits. With provider codex
and account, account-read authenticates a current read-only provider catalog.
That read requests account/read refreshToken=false and paginated model/list;
it starts no thread or inference and is never a passing model-call receipt.

To select managed future launches, a lead first reads the current revision and
uses account-select with provider, account and expectedRevision. A new Codex
selection MUST supply model: the exact current account-advertised model string.
There is no implicit model/default, credit fallback, alternate account or
automatic reroute. active:false clears only that provider's future selection.
Workers cannot read/select accounts through these lead-only controls.

Selection validates identity, access-only delivery, canonical single-holder
custody, actual subscription allowance and disabled spending. The provider's
actual exhaustion flags or 100% refuse. Valid 95%, 99% and 99.99% remain usable;
rounded display values and advisory pacing thresholds never exhaust a route.
Missing/malformed/stale allowance or identity and unknown/enabled spending
refuse. Inherited authentication/endpoint overrides are not silently replaced.

New Codex ordinary work needs current authenticated catalog, identity, allowance
and custody, NOT any past completed call, cached model table or model-policy
registry. A missing model-policy file does not block first ordinary work. The
actual child checks its catalog, usage and custody again before thread admission
and confirms the exact model before a turn can be submitted. A provider refusal
is retained as a failure, without retrying a different route.

Account admission's completionStatus is not-observed until an authenticated
provider completion from the bound thread/turn is observed. lastAttempt records
succeeded, failed, startup-refused or not-confirmed separately; lastSuccess is
created only on observed success and survives a later failure. Selection,
catalog read, admission and startup never set realCallPassed. The old legacy
proof-only helper remains for compatibility with previously pinned legacy
routes; new Codex selections always use explicit ordinary-work admission.

Once bound, a conversation retains its account, home and thread through future
selection changes/clears and resumes. Existing threads keep their inherited
home. No transcript or credential is migrated by the account control. Both the
provider child and its Fleet MCP inherit the selected account home; the lead's
home stays intact. SQLite stores selection and per-worker evidence using the
existing schema, with revision/transaction rollback on failure.

The service bridge and canonical custody files are private code-only artifacts
in the companion account-artifacts packet, qualified together with this source.
Tests accept FLEET_TEST_ACCOUNT_SERVICE pointing to the extracted service/src;
the delivery layout also supports ../account-artifacts/service/src. No account
home, token or credential belongs in a source/build packet.

Activation is a separate lead-owned operation, currently NOT performed. See the
companion ACTIVATION-ROLLBACK.txt for exact proposed paths, current baseline
hashes, same-daemon/lock and access-only delivery requirements. Existing V3
routes may be used while managed-account activation remains pending. No second
review, timer, coordinator replacement or V2 deployment is required by this port.

Custody deployment configuration is explicit: TELOGINS_CODEX_CUSTODY_CONFIG
names the existing configuration, and TELOGINS_CODEX_CUSTODY_HOST pins its
expected SSH host. Missing or mismatched host pins refuse before SSH. Use the
canonical custody host for your deployment; Fleet embeds no machine identity.
